AdapterBase.description: The base model an adapter is bound to. An adapter applied to a different base produces undefined behaviour rather than a worse answer, which is why miLLM refuses the mismatch instead of warning.

manifest_sha256.description: Hash of the base checkpoint's manifest, so the exact base stays identifiable if its directory moves. Null when the base was not itself a saved checkpoint.
manifest_sha256.title: Manifest Sha256

name.description:
The base's fully qualified name. TWO CASES, and both are defined because the sibling field permits both:

1. The base IS a saved checkpoint -> its own checkpoint manifest's 'name'.
2. The base is a Hugging Face Hub model -> THE HUB REPO ID, e.g. 'LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct'. 'manifest_sha256' is null in this case, which is what distinguishes it.

A consumer resolves the base in that order: by 'manifest_sha256' when it is present (the exact base, even if its directory moved), otherwise by matching this name against a registered repo id, otherwise against a row name.

Case 2 was ADDED 2026-10-14, raised by the miLLM session implementing adapter serving. The previous wording defined this field only as 'as its own checkpoint manifest's name gives it' - which presupposes the base is a saved checkpoint, while 'manifest_sha256' immediately below it says 'null when the base was not itself a saved checkpoint'. So THIS OBJECT EXPLICITLY ADMITTED A HUB BASE AND THEN GAVE ITS name FIELD NO DEFINED VALUE for that case - and a standalone adapter trained on a Hub model is the ordinary case, not an edge one. Same shape as the fields this project has repeatedly found asserted against a source that did not support them, caught here by a consumer trying to implement the match rather than by re-reading the schema.
name.title: Name

AdapterBase.title: AdapterBase

AdapterConfig.description: The low-rank adapter's shape and how it is applied. Rank, alpha, target modules and dropout are run configuration (BRD-02 R-02.43).

dropout.description: Dropout applied to the adapter during training. Recorded because it changes what was trained, not what is served.
dropout.title: Dropout

scaling.description: How the adapter's contribution is scaled at apply time. 'alpha_over_r' means alpha divided by rank, the PEFT default. This field exists so a different rule (for example rank-stabilised scaling) is expressible in a later schema version without changing what v1 means: a reader that does not recognise the value MUST refuse the adapter rather than guess, because guessing the scale silently changes the model's behaviour.
scaling.title: Scaling

target_modules.description: Module paths the adapter was attached to, as the model names them. miLLM refuses an adapter whose target modules or shapes do not match the resident base (BRD-01 R-01.27), and this is the field it checks against.
target_modules.title: Target Modules

AdapterConfig.title: AdapterConfig

AdapterManifestV1.description:
The manifest written beside an adapter's tensors by every adapter save (BRD-02 R-02.44). miForge owns this schema and is normative for it; miLLM vendors it byte-identical with a sync test (BRD-01 R-01.28) because it serves adapters (R-01.27). This is deliberately NOT the checkpoint manifest: that schema's fields describe a full parameter set, and an adapter is a different artifact with a mandatory base.

ON-DISK LAYOUT IS NORMATIVE. An adapter directory contains THREE files: 'adapter_model.safetensors' (the tensors), 'adapter_config.json' (PEFT's own configuration) and 'adapter_manifest.json' (this document).

'adapter_config.json' was ADDED 2026-10-14 and its absence was a defect, not a simplification: PeftConfig.from_pretrained READS THAT FILE, so a directory matching the previously-enumerated layout exactly was NOT loadable by the standard tooling R-02.51 promises, and BRD acceptance criterion 15 could not pass. It is the same shape as the tokenizer-subdirectory defect - an artifact layout that satisfied this suite's own prose and no actual loader - and the third time the adapter path had produced one. Found by checking the layout against what `peft` reads rather than by re-reading the layout. This document remains additive: it is miForge's record beside PEFT's, never a replacement for it. Tensor keys follow the PEFT convention, 'base_model.model.<module>.lora_A.weight' and '.lora_B.weight', so an adapter is loadable by standard tooling and not only by this suite.

adapter.description: The adapter's shape and scaling rule.

base.description: The base model this adapter was trained against. MANDATORY: an adapter is meaningless without it, and miLLM refuses an adapter against a different base (BRD-01 R-01.27).

name.description: The fully qualified adapter name, '<base_model>:<run_id>:adapter-<step>', with step UNPADDED — the same display rule the checkpoint manifest's 'name' follows (BRD-01 R-01.24: paths pad to six digits, names do not). The 'adapter-' segment is what distinguishes an adapter from a checkpoint of the same run and step in the tree (BRD-02 R-02.29).
name.title: Name

optimizer.description: Which optimizer produced this adapter step, and whether its state was carried in or started fresh.

parts.description: Contract references of the pack parts this adapter trained on, each '{type, name, version}' per miDataworks' handoff contract, or an external part's provenance (BRD-02 R-02.35, R-02.40). Unlike the checkpoint manifest, this artifact DOES carry them: an adapter is small, portable and routinely moved between installations, so it has to be able to say what it was trained on without its run log.
parts.title: Parts

retention.description: The out-of-domain score at this step (BRD-02 R-02.17).
retention.title: Retention

run_id.description: The adapter run that produced this.
run_id.title: Run Id

step.description: The canonical step integer, as the checkpoint manifest defines it (BRD-01 R-01.24): paths render it zero-padded to six digits, 'name' renders it unpadded. Nothing carries the step as a string of its own.
step.title: Step

test.description: The in-domain score at this step (BRD-02 R-02.16, R-02.18).
test.title: Test

weights_sha256.description: Hash of 'adapter_model.safetensors'. REQUIRED, and added because BRD-01 R-01.27 obliges miLLM to verify an adapter's hash the way R-01.14 verifies a checkpoint's weights_sha256 — a verification that had no field to read until this schema existed. Without it R-01.27 is unimplementable and a corrupted adapter loads silently.
weights_sha256.title: Weights Sha256

AdapterManifestV1.title: AdapterManifestV1

OptimizerIdentity.description: Which optimizer produced a step, and the provenance of its state. Same shape as the checkpoint manifest's, so consumers can share code.

state.description: 'restored' when optimizer state was loaded for the resumed step, 'fresh' when a new optimizer was started.
state.title: State

OptimizerIdentity.title: OptimizerIdentity

ScoreRecord.description: A score against a named evaluation set at one step. Same shape as the checkpoint manifest's.

floor.description: The value the run stops below. Set for retention (BRD-02 R-02.25); normally null for test.
floor.title: Floor

provider.description: Written by the trainer. Which inference provider produced this score (BRD-02 R-02.16, R-02.49): a score is only comparable against another taken the same way. Null when the provider was not recorded.
provider.title: Provider

set.description: Identifier of the evaluation set that produced this score.
set.title: Set

ScoreRecord.title: ScoreRecord
